notes:
Every shape sits inside one group with transform="translate(0,16)", so on-screen y is 16 more than the numbers in "d"/"cy". No shape is drawn twice: there is exactly ONE silhouette (13, the 28-arc bumpy fur blob) and no stroke-only overlay copy of it. Shapes 5-8 are the only fill:none stroke-only paths — they are the toe lines on the feet, not outline overlays.

ARMS are NOT mirrored: 9+10 (x 18-145) is a raised arm going up-left from the shoulder at (145,262) to a mitten hand at the top-left, while 11+12 (x 359-480) hangs down-right from (359,420) to a hand at (440,465). Same construction, opposite pose, so each arm needs its own drawing. LEGS are effectively mirrored: leg 3 spans x 164-244 and leg 4 spans x 279-355 (mirror of 3 about x=260 would be 276-356), and the four toe lines pair up 186<->334 and 222<->300, with only tiny jitter in the arc radii (40x80 vs 38x78) and y (418 vs 422).

Shapes 34 and 35 (#C7481A) are the one judgement call: two thin arched crescents drawn LAST, one just above each eyeball and entirely outside it (both lie beyond the white circles' radii). I read them as eyebrows, hence EYES. Two things argue for that over "fur shading": they are one-per-eye directly above the eyes, and the fur gradient lights the creature from the upper-left, so a dark shading patch would belong on the lower-right, not up here. Note they slope the same way (both rising to the right) instead of being mirrored, so they are an expressive tilt, not a mirrored pair. If the game would rather treat them as fur shading, they move to BODY as a block and nothing else changes.

Colour notes for repainting: the base orange appears three ways — the gradient url(#fur) on the silhouette, the flat #FF8A47 on the upper arms (same as the gradient's middle stop), and the lighter #FFA45C on the hands; all three must move together. #F2672A is both the gradient's dark end stop and the flat fill of the middle spike (2). There are three darker oranges at different depths: #F0702D (feet), #F2672A (middle spike), #C7481A (brows). The pale family is url(#belly) + #FFC492 (highlight patch on the upper-left of the silhouette) + #FFC08A (two freckles on the belly); #F8C795 is the shading arc under the belly, so it is the pale family's own shade — I tagged it "dark" to flag that it must stay a step deeper than the belly, otherwise a repaint makes it vanish. The horn cream url(#horn) is an accent shared by both horns (0, 1), while the middle spike (2) is base-coloured, not horn-coloured. Fixed colours that must never be repainted: #0B1B3B outline, #FFFFFF (one tooth 23, two eyeballs, four catchlights), #FF9E9E cheeks, #A8355A mouth cavity, #FF93AD tongue, #6CD3DE irises, #16294F pupils. The mouth has only ONE tooth (23), on the screen-left side.
